By now we should all be somewhat familiar with Putt's philosophy of ebb and flow—arguably a very important philosophy to have when involved in software development. The way I interpret this idea is: one goes about working hard for a certain amount of time without any real breaks or relaxation, and after certain milestones are met, or certain amounts of time have been invested, one will break and do no work at all for some amount of time. Imagine working 18 hour days on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday and then having the rest of the week off, ad infinitum.

There is no set amount of time to work or relax that I know of, and one thing we know from past experience is that even when Putt is utterly silent and no signs of presence are visible at all, he is often still working hard behind the scenes addressing issues or developing new features.

For a number of weeks in a row Putt was very active on the preview site developing new features that are intended to fix a large number of functionality issues on Voat (including subverse transfers).
